recruits.name: Dan Okafor
recruits.backstory: Construction site foreman in Lagos for a decade—kept crews safe, kept budgets real, kept politicians honest when he could. Here, he does the exact same job but with a shield instead of a clipboard. The crews are smaller and greener, but the work's the same: stand in front so your people don't have to. He's not adapting so much as finally doing what he was always meant to do.
recruits.greeting: You're putting a group together? Good. Somebody's got to stand at the front.
recruits.home_note: At the drill grounds in Valley of Strength.

recruits.name: Ama Boateng
recruits.backstory: Paediatric nurse in Lagos for eleven years. Night shifts, cots instead of beds, malaria and malnutrition and the weight of knowing you can't save them all. She rolled healers in every game she ever touched—that was a tell nobody listened to. Here, light comes from her hands instead of prayer, patients are green instead of brown, and there's no turning people away. The weight's different but just as heavy. She hasn't adapted. She's just finally working somewhere the job makes sense.
recruits.greeting: I've kept people breathing on worse nights than this. Stay in my line of sight.
recruits.home_note: Set up in the infirmary tent.

recruits.name: Silas Vance
recruits.backstory: Port security in Antwerp, five years watching cargo and watching people. Never took a side in the dockside games, never committed to anything. Got paid well, kept his head down, stayed clean. Then the frontier happened and he came looking for chaos—figured a fresh world meant fresh options. Turned out chaos has more rules than he expected, and the code here is cleaner than anything in Antwerp. He's not adapting to a new world. He's relieved to finally find one that makes sense.
recruits.greeting: You want someone who hits things, or someone who hits things before they notice? Different rates.
recruits.home_note: At the docks, leaning on a crate like he owns it.

recruits.name: Rosa Delgado
recruits.backstory: Hunting guide in Tanzania for eight years. Tracked lions for researchers, photographed leopards, understood that predators have ethics and hunger is honest. Then she got here and found something wilder—thinking prey that shoots back. Learning to aim at targets that plan is harder than aiming at targets that flee. She misses the savanna every day. But the frontier's wilder, and she came here looking for wild. She's not adapting. She's home, just farther from the ocean.
recruits.greeting: Do you have any idea what's living out here? No? Then yes, I'm coming with you.
recruits.home_note: At the treeline with her kill hung.

recruits.name: Marco Rossi
recruits.backstory: Police officer in Milan for twelve years—stood between neighborhoods and chaos, wore the badge, believed in order. The frontier took that away and gave him light magic instead. Now he stands between the forsaken and judgment. The job's the same, the uniform's just invisible. He's not adapting. He's still standing between worlds.
recruits.greeting: Order is a choice we make every day. Let me help you make it.
recruits.home_note: In the Royal Quarter, keeping the peace.

recruits.name: Sophia Dias
recruits.backstory: Physics researcher in São Paulo, Brazil—ten years studying combustion in industrial accidents, writing reports governments ignored, watching factories burn from the safe side of data. Fire magic is just applied physics, and she burns brighter here. Now people actually care about her research. The frontier didn't change the work. It finally made the work matter.
recruits.greeting: Show me something that burns and I'll tell you why.
recruits.home_note: In the Magic Quarter, surrounded by research.

recruits.name: Ryan Murphy
recruits.backstory: Stock broker in Boston, twelve years cutting deals that hurt people quietly. Made money, lost sleep, drank too much after work. The frontier showed him summoning demons is the same skill—reading power, cutting deals, understanding what things want. At least the demons are honest about their price. He's not adapting. He's finally being honest about what he always was.
recruits.greeting: Everything costs something. The question is what you're willing to pay.
recruits.home_note: In the Warlock Quarter, making deals.

recruits.name: Carolina Santos
recruits.backstory: Environmentalist in Peru, spent twelve years protecting rainforest and fighting mining corporations with nothing but data and rage. Shamanism came to her like a language she already spoke—the earth was always talking, she just finally had the words. Now she stands at Echo Isles' springs and listens to what the frontier is trying to say. She's not adapting. She's finally being heard.
recruits.greeting: The land speaks if you know how to listen. Let me teach you.

recruits.name: Amber Whitehorse
recruits.backstory: Ranger and biologist from Alberta, Canada—spent fifteen years managing national forests, knowing the land, and watching bureaucrats make decisions that destroyed it anyway. Druidry made sense instantly—it's land stewardship with teeth. Now she measures progress in weeks instead of years and the forests actually listen. She's not adapting. She's finally in a place where the land fights back.
recruits.greeting: The forest doesn't need saving. It needs defending. Come on.
recruits.home_note: Deep in the grove, defending the land.

recruits.name: Marcus Okafor
recruits.backstory: Meteorologist in Toronto, Canada—studied climate patterns and wrote warnings nobody in government wanted to hear. Storms were always his obsession, but he could only record them. Here he channels them. The frontier showed him the work he was always meant to do. He's not adapting. He's finally got the tools he needed.
recruits.greeting: Every storm has a story. Mine's just getting interesting.

recruits.name: Ivan Petrov
recruits.backstory: Boxer from St. Petersburg, Russia—twenty years in the ring before the frontier took him. Violence was his language and he spoke it well. Here the violence is cleaner: no judges, no politics, no disappointed family. Ragefire Chasm's heat feels right. He doesn't think about Earth much anymore. This place burns like he does and that's enough.
recruits.greeting: In the ring I fought for points. Here I fight for real. It's better.

recruits.name: Asher Coleman
recruits.backstory: Deep South, Bible Belt born and raised - you can hear it before he says three words. Says the fall into this world felt less like falling and more like being carried, though he laughs it off before it turns into a sermon. He's been camped outside the Coven for two days on his own, alone, waiting on nobody, because somebody's got to and he figures it might as well be him. Doesn't ask why you're here. Just asks if you could use the help, like it's the easiest question in the world.
recruits.greeting: Figure the Good Lord doesn't waste a resurrection on a man who's got nothing left to do with it. There's demons past that ridge. I mean to see to them. Walk with me, if you're willing.
